topic: How does the internet send a message?
title: How Does the Internet Send a Message? (Explained Like You're 5)
description: When you send a message, where does it go? Zoe sends a letter to Grandma and learns about packets, routers and servers — the internet, explained with a post office made of light.

props.question: How does the internet send a message?

lines.text: Hi friend! Have you ever sent a message on a phone?
Whoosh! It arrives in a blink.
But how does it get there? Let's find out!
This is Zoe.
Zoe wants to send a letter to her grandma.
But Grandma lives far, far away, in another town.
A paper letter takes days and days.
So the internet does something clever!
It takes Zoe's message,
and cuts it into tiny pieces.
Each tiny piece is called a packet.
The packets leave Zoe's phone.
A helper called a router points the way.
They visit a server, a big mailbox that never sleeps.
And zoom! They reach Grandma's phone.
Now imagine millions of phones, computers and helpers.
All holding hands with wires and invisible waves.
Packets zip between them all day and all night.
This giant web of helpers is called... the internet!

props.bubble: What if a packet gets lost?

lines.text: Leo asks, what if a packet gets lost?
No problem! Grandma's phone just asks for it again.
A paper letter takes days.
Internet packets take less than a second!
Zoom, zoom, zoom!

cards.means: a tiny piece of a message

lines.text: So let's remember!
A packet is a tiny piece of a message.
A router points the way.
And a server is a big mailbox that never sleeps.
Great job today, friend! Send Grandma a hug!
